idea.title: GPT‑6.1 Terra vs Top Agents
idea.the_news: OpenAI launched GPT‑6.1 Terra, touting stronger agent abilities and opened API access.
idea.what_you_do: I ran a 20‑task agent benchmark (code generation, web‑scraping, VM control) using GPT‑6.1 Terra, GPT‑6 Luna, GPT‑6 Sol, and Groq’s 120B OSS model.
idea.post_shows: Scoreboard {{result}} highlights where Terra shines, where it trips, plus latency and cost per task.
idea.why_hired: Demonstrates I can evaluate frontier models for production‑ready agents.
idea.why_hot: Founders see I can vet the newest LLMs before they become mainstream.
idea.role_angle: I know how to benchmark and pick the right LLM for agent pipelines.
idea.build_plan: 1. Grab OpenAI API key for Terra (beta). 2. Write Python harness that sends same prompt to each model. 3. Record success/failure, latency, token usage. 4. Summarize in a table and write post.
hook_options: I pitted GPT‑6.1 Terra against the best agents – the winner surprised me.
20 real‑world agent tasks: does Terra finally beat the competition?
idea.visual: table comparing pass/fail, latency (s), $ per task for each model
needs: OpenAI API access to GPT‑6.1 Terra (beta)

option.short_title: One‑click UI mockup generator with GPT‑6.1 Terra
option.what_it_is: A lightweight Next.js web app that accepts a hand‑drawn sketch, calls the Terra Agent API (openai:gpt‑6.1‑sol) to (1) interpret the sketch, (2) write a React component tree, and (3) serve a live preview. All code is generated on‑the‑fly and deployed to Vercel.
option.what_you_show: A 45‑second screen‑recording: upload a doodle → React UI appears in seconds, plus a public GitHub repo link.
option.why_hired: Shows I can take a brand‑new frontier model, turn it into a shipped product feature in an afternoon, and handle prompt‑engineering, API integration, and production deployment end‑to‑end.
option.twist: Most viral demos stop at static images; I close the loop by producing runnable code and a live preview – exactly what a startup needs to ship.
option.title: Demo‑App
option.inspired_by: YouTube video “GPT‑6.1 Terra is now in orbit” (531 k views)
option.your_edge: Built the full UI pipeline, added error‑handling and a cost‑monitor, kept total API spend under $3.
option.what_you_build: Next.js front‑end + tiny Python/Node shim that talks to Terra’s agent mode.
option.why_hiring_cares: Speed of delivery, production‑grade integration, and cost awareness.
option.who_it_impresses: Founders looking for engineers who can prototype and ship with the newest models fast.
option.stand_out: Turns a hype‑driven image generation demo into a real, runnable product component.
option.difficulty: medium – wiring the agent, handling file I/O, and deploying.
option.difficulty_why: Requires prompt‑engineering, API auth, and a small CI/CD pipeline.
option.risk: Paid API required; kept under $3 by limiting token usage.
option.hook: I fed a hand‑drawn sketch to GPT‑6.1 Terra and got a live React UI in seconds – {{result}}
